title: security: RBAC v2 - enforce KMS region pinning + audit logging hardening
author: Aisha Verma
release_notes: Hardening for RBAC v2: enforce customer KMS region pinning for key-bound resources and improve audit logging for policy decisions. No API changes; opt-in via admin flag and rolling migration.
description: Context: We need to close a set of compliance gaps identified during an internal audit and a customer review (SUP-2123). Current RBAC v2 allows KMS-backed resources to be referenced without strict region residency enforcement and audit trails for KMS policy decisions are sparse. This PR enforces region pinning for KMS-backed resources at the policy evaluation layer and hardens audit logging for both policy decisions and KMS key access. Motivation: ensure data residency guarantees and provide reliable evidence for audits while preventing cross-region KMS misuse. Summary of changes: 1) RBAC policy evaluator: add 'kms_region' attribute check and failure mode. Policies requesting KMS operations on resources with pinned regions will be denied unless request context includes matching kms_region. 2) KMS integration: runtime now annotates requests with resolved key_region and key_id; we introduce a lightweight KMS metadata cache to avoid extra RPCs on hot paths. 3) Audit logging: every authorization decision that involves KMS or region constraints now emits a standardized audit event (rbac_v2.policy_decision) including principal, action, resource, requested_kms_region, resolved_kms_region, policy_id, decision, and reason. 4) Migration and rollout: introduce admin flag 'rbac_v2.enforce_kms_region_pinning' (default: false) and a rollout job to detect misaligned policies; a follow-up job will auto-annotate obvious mismatches using a safe-preview mode. 5) Tests and docs: unit and integration tests for policy evaluator, KMS cache tests, e2e test simulating a cross-region request; docs updated in security/rbac-v2.md. Checklist: - [x] Add kms_region attribute to policy schema and evaluator logic - [x] Emit structured audit events for policy decisions involving KMS - [x] Introduce KMS metadata cache with TTL and metrics - [x] Admin feature flag and migration job (safe-preview) - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Security review and threat model update - [x] Docs and release notes Changeset: commits listed below. Files changed (high level): - rbac/policy/evaluator.go: policy attribute handling, logging hooks - rbac/policy/schema.yaml: kms_region attribute documentation - integrations/kms/client.go: annotate resolved key metadata and cache - integrations/kms/cache.go: new simple TTL cache and metrics hooks - observability/audit/producer.go: new audit event schema and emitters - cmd/migrations/enforce_kms_region_preview.go: migration job and safe-preview CLI - tests/integration/test_kms_region_pinning.go: end-to-end scenarios - docs/security/rbac-v2.md: migration and admin flag guide Review notes: This change touches the critical auth path. Performance impact was profiled: adding the KMS metadata cache keeps additional latency on the hot path under +1.8ms p95 in our perf canary with a 500ms KMS RPC fallback. The cache is bounded with LRU and a default TTL of 30s; metrics exported: kms_cache.hit, kms_cache.miss, kms_cache.evictions. Backwards compatibility: The enforcement is opt-in via the admin flag. We validate policies at migration time and provide a non-destructive safe-preview that only emits findings to the audit log. Rollout plan included in docs. Security considerations: - Ensure audit events do not include plaintext key material; only key_id and region are logged. - KMS client uses existing tenant-scoped credentials; no new secrets. - Threat model updated; mitigation for attacker attempting to spoof kms_region by requiring both request metadata and KMS-resolved metadata to match. How to test manually: - Enable flag in dev control plane, deploy policy that pins resource to us-west-2, simulate a request coming from us-east-1 with key in us-east-1; expect DENY and audit event with reason 'kms_region_mismatch'. Commits: see commit list below. CI: All checks passed on second run after fixing linter warnings and a transient integration test flake. Merge: squash and merge to main after approvals.
